title: Passport to Product: 30-day engineer onboarding canvas
body:
Purpose: a single, lightweight working canvas to accelerate new engineers’ product orientation and early impact in the first 30 days. Focus is cross-functional rhythm (product + eng + design + people-ops). This doc is intentionally practical: checklists, week-by-week milestones, interview/ramp signals for hiring calibration, and a short feedback loop for mentor handoffs.

Quick context / why different: most onboarding playbooks focus on accesses and tech setup. Passport-to-Product centers the product mental model first so new hires can ship meaningful changes quickly and ask better technical questions. Useful for IC hires (E, E+), contractor-to-perm, and lateral transfers into platform/product teams.

High-level goals (first 30 days):
- Goal A: Understand product surface and core user workflows; run the product locally and complete a feature walkthrough with PM + designer.
- Goal B: Commit one small, production-safe change (bugfix, test, doc, config) that touches the codepath end-to-end.
- Goal C: Establish a steady weekly sync with mentor and two cross-functional stakeholders.
- Goal D: Clear basic infra/access checklist and shadow at least one oncall/bug-triage rotation.

Owner / roles
- People Ops: Priya Kapoor (owner) — onboarding flow, access gating cadence, pulse check at day 7/15/30.
- Mentor: assigned by hiring manager on offer acceptance — weekly 1:1 + daily async triage channel.
- Hiring manager: responsible for role-specific goals, first 30-day sprint card in Jira, and final sign-off at day 30.
- Cross-functional stakeholders: Product (PM), Design, SRE/Infra (if relevant) — each to run a 45m orientation session in week 1.

Before day 0 (offer -> start) checklist (people-ops tasks)
- Confirm start date and timezone.
- Send preboarding packet: org map, team charter, high-level product read (5 pages), quick security FAQ.
- Hardware & accounts: laptop shipped, VPN profile assigned, SSO invite, GitHub org invite, Slack, Jira.
- Mentor assigned and intro note sent (mentor + hire + hiring manager cc).
- Create first-week calendar skeleton: day0 orientation, product tour, repo setup, code walkthrough.
- Suggested prework for hire: product primer (15m), repo README (15m), onboarding checklist doc with links.

Day 0 to Day 7 — week 0 checklist (orientation + low-friction wins)
- Day 0: 30–60m welcome + HR/benefits + logistics with people-ops.
- Day 1: 45m team kickoff (team mission + roadmap + immediate priorities).
- Day 1: product tour with PM + 30m design teardown.
- Day 1–3: dev environment provisioning: run local build, run tests, open first dev PR template.
- Create 30-day Jira card and link to manager’s acceptance criteria.
- Shadow triage channel for 1 full day (observe pager flow).
- Deliverable: open an infrastructure-safe PR (typo/doc/test).

Week 2 (days 8–14) — product & code ramp
- Deep-dive walkthrough of key repo (owner-led, 60–90m).
- Pair on a small bug or tech debt task with mentor.
- PM/Designer: set expectations for feature delivery cycle (spec -> PR -> QA).
- Checkpoint: manager runs a progress 1:1 and adjusts the 30-day card.

Week 3 (days 15–21) — first feature loop
- New hire owns a scoped change: spec, PR, address reviews, merge to staging.
- Run a short post-merge verification checklist (smoke test + basic metric sanity).
- Mini presentation (15–20m) to team: what I changed, why, open questions.
- People-ops pulse survey (3 quick questions) at day 21.

Week 4 (days 22–30) — close loop + signals
- Finish any outstanding reviews, tests, docs.
- Manager + mentor + hire retrospective: readiness to move from onboarding to normal cadence.
- Sign-off criteria: product tour demonstrated; one end-to-end merged change; mentor confirms baseline independence.
- Celebration: 30-day note to team + next-steps card for 60/90 day goals.

Access & infra gating list (minimum)
- SSO + Slack + email + Google Drive.
- GitHub org + repo-level write access (initially triage or PR rights as appropriate).
- CI/CD pipeline read + deploy request flow (deploy permission gated).
- VPN + VPC read-only on day 1; escalation for infra changes.
- Oncall rotation added as shadow; write access after manager approval.

Mentor rotation protocol (short)
- Week 0: mentor introduces repo and acceptance criteria for a small task.
- Week 1–2: daily short async check-ins on PR progress.
- Week 3: reduce pairing; mentor reviews PR and ensures the hire can independently triage.
- Handoff notes: mentor fills a 1-paragraph readiness statement at day 30.

Interview & hiring calibration artifacts (compact rubric to keep hiring signal consistent)
- Purpose: provide a short rubric hiring managers can reuse when calibrating interviewers; aligns ramp expectations to level.
- Structure (score 1–4):
  - Problem decomposition (can break product requirement into technical tasks).
  - System design breadth (practical tradeoffs for chosen approach).
  - Code quality & ownership (tests, docs, simple refactor).
  - Communication & cross-team collaboration (pairing + synthesizing feedback).
- Quick guidance: a candidate scoring 3 or above across majority and with clear product curiosity = hire for this product-forward onboarding track.

Sample interview prompts (for hiring managers to copy):
- "Describe a time you shipped a small but meaningful product fix under time constraints. How did you decide scope?"
- "Given this simplified user flow (link to product primer), what would you test locally first and why?"
- "Walk me through how you'd debug a 10% regression in an existing metric after a deployment."

Signals for readiness to graduate from onboarding (day 30 pass/fail style)
- Must-have signals (all required):
  - Completed E2E change merged to staging with verification steps run.
  - Presented outcome to team.
  - Can explain the main product workflows for the area.
- Nice-to-have signals:
  - Opened an improvement ticket and triaged next actions.
  - Independent small triage in production shadow.

Asynchronous artifacts to produce by day 30 (templates)
- One-slide "what I accomplished" summary.
- Short onboarding notes for next hire (what failed, what helped).
- One-line mentor readiness statement.

Risks & mitigations (notes to people-ops)
- Risk: under-scoped first task becomes a blocker -> mitigation: define strict acceptance criteria and timebox.
- Risk: infra access delay -> mitigation: escalate to infra owner, provide read-only alternatives.
- Risk: mentor bandwidth mismatch -> mitigation: fallback mentoring policy (second mentor from another pod).

Open questions / TODOs
- Add a one-page product primer template for each team (product-led one-pager including 2 metrics, 2 user stories).
- Align with security on deploy gating policy for contractors vs full-time.
- Build small Notion/Confluence macro to auto-generate 30-day Jira card from offer data.

Quick templates (copy/paste)
- 30-day Jira card title: "ONBOARD: [Name] — 30d product passport — [team]"
- Mentor readiness snippet: "[Mentor name] confirms [hire] can independently run local build, open a PR, and explain product flow for [area]."

Notes to self (Priya)
- Keep doc intentionally short — embed links not long text.
- Pilot with 3 hires in Q4 and measure: time-to-first-merge, manager confidence score, and hire NPS at day 30.

Related references
- Confluence: onboarding master checklist (linked above).
- People-ops pulse survey template: PULSE-2025-Q3.
- Hiring rubric canonical doc: HIRING-RUBRIC-ENG.

End of canvas. This is a living draft — please leave inline comments or add to the TODO section.
